import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture

The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture on $\chi$-boundedness of graphs with a forbidden induced tree.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C3%A1rf%C3%A1s%E2%80%93Sumner_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gy75] A. Gyárfás, *On Ramsey covering-numbers*, Infinite and finite sets (Colloq., Keszthely,
  1973), Vol. II, North-Holland, 1975.
- [Su81] D. P. Sumner, *Subtrees of a graph and the chromatic number*, The theory and applications
  of graphs (Kalamazoo, Mich., 1980), Wiley, 1981.
-/

namespace GyarfasSumnerConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
**Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.** For any fixed pair of a tree $T$ and a complete graph $K_t$, the
graphs that are both $T$-free and $K_t$-free are $\chi$-bounded. That is, for every finite tree
$T$ and every $t$, there is a constant $c$ (depending only on $T$ and $t$) such that every finite
graph $G$ containing neither $T$ nor $K_t$ as an induced subgraph satisfies $\chi(G) \le c$.

Here `T ⊴ G` means that `G` has an induced subgraph isomorphic to `T` (there is a graph embedding
`T ↪g G`), and `G.CliqueFree t` means that `G` has no clique on `t` vertices, i.e. no induced
subgraph isomorphic to $K_t$. A tree is a connected acyclic graph, so `T` is nonempty.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem gyarfas_sumner_conjecture {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (T : SimpleGraph α) (hT : T.IsTree)
    (t : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ {β : Type*} [Fintype β] (G : SimpleGraph β),
      ¬ T ⊴ G → G.CliqueFree t → G.chromaticNumber ≤ c := by
  sorry

end GyarfasSumnerConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the source: the list entry names one conjecture, and the article's 'equivalent' phrasing and known special cases are not separate questions.
modeling_decisions: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the article's lead: ∀ tree T, ∀ t, ∃ c, ∀ G (T-free and K_t-free ⇒ χ(G) ≤ c). This quantifier order (c depends only on T and t, not on G) is what χ-boundedness of the class means.

'T-free' is modelled as induced-subgraph-free: `¬ T ⊴ G` where `SimpleGraph.IsIndContained T G := Nonempty (T ↪g G)`; a graph embedding is exactly an isomorphism onto an induced subgraph. Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Free` (non-induced copies) was deliberately NOT used.

'K_t-free' is modelled as `G.CliqueFree t`; for complete graphs, induced and non-induced containment coincide (Mathlib: `not_cliqueFree_iff : ¬G.CliqueFree n ↔ Nonempty (completeGraph (Fin n) ↪g G)`). Degenerate t: t = 0 makes the hypothesis impossible (vacuous), t = 1 forces G empty; neither changes the mathematical content.

Trees are `SimpleGraph.IsTree` (connected and acyclic); connectedness in Mathlib includes nonemptiness, so T is nonempty and `¬ T ⊴ G` is a genuine constraint (an empty T would be inducedly contained in everything). T is required finite via `[Fintype α]`, as in the standard statement.

G is restricted to finite graphs (`[Fintype β]`), following the standard finite-graph reading (and the decomposition notes). By de Bruijn–Erdős compactness the infinite-graph version is equivalent, so nothing is lost.
The chromatic number is Mathlib's `chromaticNumber : ℕ∞`; the bound is `G.chromaticNumber ≤ (c : ℕ∞)` with c : ℕ. For a finite graph χ is finite, so this is the intended inequality.
Vertex types are universe-polymorphic (`Type*`) for both T and G; since the graphs are finite this is immaterial up to isomorphism but avoids an artificial restriction to `Type`.

Only the single slot is stated. The article's 'equivalently, every K_t-free G with χ large enough contains T induced' is the contrapositive of the same proposition and is not stated separately, per the decomposition notes.

gyarfas_sumner_conjecture.why: Stated as: for every finite tree T (SimpleGraph α, [Fintype α], T.IsTree) and every t : ℕ, there exists c : ℕ such that every finite simple graph G with no induced copy of T (¬ T ⊴ G, i.e. no graph embedding T ↪g G) and no t-clique (G.CliqueFree t) has G.chromaticNumber ≤ c. All primitives (IsTree, IsIndContained, CliqueFree, chromaticNumber) are from Mathlib; no bespoke definitions.

/-!
# Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture

The Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture says that for every fixed tree $T$ and complete graph $K_t$, the
class of graphs that contain neither $T$ nor $K_t$ as an induced subgraph is $\chi$-bounded, i.e.
every such graph can be properly colored with a number of colors depending only on $T$ and $t$.

It was formulated independently by Gyárfás (1975) and Sumner (1981) and remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C3%A1rf%C3%A1s%E2%80%93Sumner_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gy75] A. Gyárfás, *On Ramsey covering-numbers*, in: Infinite and finite sets (Colloq.,
  Keszthely, 1973), Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai 10, North-Holland, 1975, pp. 801–816.
- [Su81] D. P. Sumner, *Subtrees of a graph and the chromatic number*, in: The theory and
  applications of graphs (Kalamazoo, Mich., 1980), Wiley, New York, 1981, pp. 557–576.
-/

namespace GyarfasSumnerConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
**Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.**

For every fixed pair of a (finite) tree $T$ and a complete graph $K_t$, the class of graphs that
are both $T$-free and $K_t$-free is $\chi$-bounded. That is, for every finite tree $T$ and every
$t$, there is a constant $c$ (depending only on $T$ and $t$) such that every finite simple graph
$G$ that contains neither $T$ nor $K_t$ as an induced subgraph satisfies $\chi(G) \le c$.

Here "$T$-free" means that $G$ has no *induced* subgraph isomorphic to $T$, which we express as
`IsEmpty (T ↪g G)`: a graph embedding `T ↪g G` is an injective vertex map that preserves both
adjacency and non-adjacency. "$K_t$-free" is `G.CliqueFree t`, i.e. $G$ has no clique on $t$
vertices (for complete graphs, induced and non-induced containment coincide).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem gyarfas_sumner_conjecture :
    ∀ {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (T : SimpleGraph α), T.IsTree →
      ∀ t : ℕ, ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ {β : Type*} [Fintype β] (G : SimpleGraph β),
        IsEmpty (T ↪g G) → G.CliqueFree t → G.chromaticNumber ≤ c := by
  sorry

end GyarfasSumnerConjecture

The single-slot decomposition is correct: the list entry names one conjecture, and the article's 'equivalent' rephrasing is the contrapositive of the same proposition. The known special cases (paths, stars, radius-two trees) and the subdivision result are background theorems, not posed problems.
modeling_decisions: The list entry is terse ('χ-boundedness of graphs with a forbidden induced tree'); the precise formulation was taken from the Wikipedia article's first sentence: ∀ tree T, ∀ t, ∃ c, every graph that is T-free and K_t-free (both in the induced sense) has χ ≤ c.

'T-free' is formalized as `IsEmpty (T ↪g G)` (Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Embedding` = `RelEmbedding`, injective with `G.Adj (f a) (f b) ↔ T.Adj a b`), i.e. induced-subgraph-free. Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Free` was deliberately NOT used because it is non-induced (subgraph) containment, which would state a different (false for e.g. T = P_3 vs. complete graphs... in general a different) conjecture.

'K_t-free' is formalized as `G.CliqueFree t`; for complete graphs induced and non-induced containment coincide. Boundary: `CliqueFree 0` is unsatisfiable (the empty set is a 0-clique), so t = 0 is vacuous, which matches the mathematics (K_0 is contained in every graph); `CliqueFree 1` forces G to be empty (χ = 0). Neither changes the claim.

Trees are finite: T lives on a `[Fintype α]` vertex type and `IsTree` (connected + acyclic) forces the vertex set to be nonempty, so T is a genuine finite tree. Host graphs G are also finite (`[Fintype β]`), following the standard finite-graph setting of χ-boundedness (by De Bruijn–Erdős compactness the finite and infinite versions are equivalent for finite T anyway).

The bound c is a natural number and the conclusion is `G.chromaticNumber ≤ (c : ℕ∞)`; c is chosen after T and t but before G, so it depends only on T and t, as required. Equivalently this says the class is χ-bounded with bounding function f(t) = c(T, t).

Vertex types are quantified as `Type*` with `[Fintype]` rather than `Fin n`; the resulting theorem is universe-polymorphic in two universe variables, which is harmless since every finite graph is isomorphic to one on `Fin n`.
The article's 'Equivalently, every K_t-free graph of large enough χ contains T induced' is the contrapositive of the same statement and is not stated separately, per the decomposition table.

Quantifier order ∀ T, ∀ t, ∃ c, ∀ G matches the source. Only existing Mathlib primitives are used.
